title: Grammar: Noun Clauses — That-Clauses and Wh-Clauses
grammarTip:
Именные клаузы (Noun clauses) — клауза работает как существительное:

Как ПОДЛЕЖАЩЕЕ:
"What he said was surprising." (что он сказал = подлежащее)
"That she passed was unexpected."

Как ДОПОЛНЕНИЕ:
"I know what you did." · "She said that she was tired."
"He asked where we were going."

Как ДОПОЛНЕНИЕ К ПРИЛАГАТЕЛЬНОМУ:
"I am sure that she'll come."
"Are you aware of what happened?"

СВОДНАЯ ТАБЛИЦА вводных слов:
THAT → факт: "I know that she's right."
WHAT → "что" неизвестное: "I don't know what to do."
WHETHER/IF → альтернатива: "Ask whether she's coming."
WH-words → вопросительные слова: who, when, where, why, how

grammarTable.subject: That-clause (subject)
grammarTable.example: That misinformation spreads quickly is alarming. / That he lied is now established.

grammarTable.subject: That-clause (object)
grammarTable.short: noun clause as object of main verb
grammarTable.example: She believes that the report was accurate. / He discovered that the source was fabricated.

grammarTable.subject: It + that-clause
grammarTable.verb: It + be + adj/pp + that + S + V
grammarTable.example: It is clear that social media enables disinformation. / It has been shown that fact-checking works.

grammarTable.subject: The fact that
grammarTable.verb: The fact + that + S + V + verb phrase
grammarTable.example: The fact that only one site carried the story should raise alarm.

grammarTable.subject: Wh-clause (what/how/where/why/who/when)
grammarTable.example: What matters is the source. / I understand how algorithms work. / She knows what to look for.

grammarTable.subject: Wh-clause as subject
grammarTable.example: What concerns me most is the speed of disinformation spread. / How this happened is unclear.

rows.form: Believe, think, know, understand, realise + that
rows.example: "I believe that media literacy is essential." / "She realised that the story was fabricated."

rows.form: Claim, argue, suggest, assert, maintain + that
rows.example: "He claimed that the video was authentic." / "Critics argue that regulation is needed."

rows.form: Show, prove, find, discover, demonstrate + that
rows.example: "Research has shown that emotional content spreads faster." / "The data demonstrates that the filter bubble effect is real."

rows.form: Fear, hope, worry, suspect, expect + that
rows.example: "Many fear that disinformation will undermine democracy." / "She suspected that the account was a bot."

rows.form: It is clear / obvious / apparent / evident + that
rows.example: "It is clear that the story was fabricated." / "It is evident that the site is partisan."

rows.form: It is important / essential / necessary / vital + that
rows.example: "It is essential that citizens develop media literacy skills."

rows.form: It has been shown / found / established + that
rows.example: "It has been established that the accounts were bots." / "It has been found that corrections reach fewer people than false claims."

rows.form: It is alleged / reported / claimed + that (passive)
rows.example: "It is alleged that the government used bots to manipulate discourse." / "It was reported that the video was a deepfake."

grammarExtra.title: The Fact That: Noun Phrase + That-Clause

rows.form: The fact that + S + V
rows.example: "The fact that the story was shared 10,000 times before being corrected is deeply concerning."

rows.form: Despite the fact that / In spite of the fact that
rows.example: "Despite the fact that the article was debunked, it is still circulating online."

rows.form: Given the fact that / Bearing in mind the fact that
rows.example: "Given the fact that outlets are under financial pressure, quality has declined."

rows.form: The fact that cannot begin a sentence easily — use "It is a fact that" or reorder
rows.example: "It is a fact that media ownership is increasingly concentrated."

grammarExtra.title: Wh-Clauses: What, How, Why, Who, Where, When

rows.form: What + S + V = the thing that (subject or object)
rows.example: "What matters is the source's track record." / "Tell me what you found."

rows.form: How + S + V = the way in which
rows.example: "Understanding how algorithms determine what we see is important."

rows.form: Why + S + V = the reason
rows.example: "We need to understand why emotional content spreads faster."

rows.form: Who + S + V / Who + V = the person who
rows.example: "The question of who owns the media matters enormously." / "She doesn't know who wrote the article."

rows.form: ❌ She believes the story is false. (missing "that" — ambiguous)
rows.example: ✅ She believes that the story is false. (explicit "that" is clearer in formal writing)

rows.form: ❌ What I wonder is that she said. (wrong connector)
rows.example: ✅ What I wonder is what she said. / I wonder what she said.

rows.form: ❌ It is clear what disinformation is dangerous.
rows.example: ✅ It is clear that disinformation is dangerous. (use "that" after "it is clear")

rows.form: ❌ The fact that he said, it was false.
rows.example: ✅ The fact that he said it was false... / The fact that what he said was false... (restructure)

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct connector for the noun clause.
exercises.text: "It is clear ___ social media has changed how information spreads."
exercises.hint: "It is clear that + clause" — standard that-clause pattern

exercises.text: "Researchers have found ___ emotional content is shared more widely than neutral content."
"___ concerns me most is the concentration of media ownership in a few hands."
exercises.hint: "What concerns me is…" = wh-clause as grammatical subject

exercises.text: "The fact ___ corrections reach fewer people than false claims is well documented."
exercises.hint: "The fact that + clause" = noun phrase + that-clause

exercises.text: "She realised ___ the account was automated — it was a bot."
exercises.hint: "Realised that + clause" = discovery reporting verb + that-clause

exercises.text: "Understanding ___ algorithms decide what to show us is the first step in media literacy."
exercises.hint: "How + S + V" = the mechanism/way in which

opts: It is essential that media literacy teaching in schools.
It is essential that media literacy is taught in schools.
It is essential what media literacy is taught in schools.
It is essential if media literacy is taught in schools.
exercises.correct: It is essential that media literacy is taught in schools.
exercises.hint: "It is essential that + S + V" — standard pattern with that-clause

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct noun clause pattern.
exercises.text: "The government claimed ___ the report contained no errors — but fact-checkers disagreed."
exercises.hint: "Claimed that + clause" — that-clause after a reporting verb

exercises.text: "I don't understand ___ this story reached so many people before being corrected."
"___ he stated publicly and ___ the data actually showed were two very different things."
exercises.hint: "What + S + V" = the thing that (used twice as noun clause subjects)

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct noun clause pattern.
exercises.text: "Despite the fact ___ the article was debunked, it continued to circulate."
exercises.hint: "Despite the fact that + clause" — concessive noun phrase + that-clause

exercises.text: "It has been demonstrated ___ fact-checking can reduce belief in false claims by up to 40%."
exercises.hint: "It has been demonstrated that" = formal passive + that-clause

exercises.instruction: Which sentence uses the wh-clause correctly?
opts: "I know that what she is doing."
exercises.hint: "Know + what + S + V" — no inversion in embedded clauses

exercises.text: "It is alleged ___ foreign governments used bots to interfere in the election."
exercises.hint: "It is alleged that + clause" — passive reporting + that-clause

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct sentence for formal writing.
exercises.text: Choose the most formal and correct version:
opts: "That propaganda works is shown by history."
exercises.hint: "Shows that + clause" — subject + reporting verb + that-clause (most natural in formal writing)

exercises.instruction: What is wrong with this sentence?
exercises.text: "It is clear what disinformation spreads faster than corrections."
exercises.hint: "It is clear that + clause" — use "that" after evaluative expressions, not "what"

questions.text: "It is clear ___ the media landscape has changed fundamentally in the digital age."
questions.hint: "It is clear that + clause" — standard noun clause after evaluative expression

questions.text: "Researchers have demonstrated ___ emotional content spreads faster than factual reporting."
"___ concerns me is the lack of independent local journalism in many regions."
questions.hint: "What concerns me is…" = wh-clause as grammatical subject

questions.text: "The fact ___ newsrooms have been dramatically downsized has serious implications for democracy."
questions.hint: "The fact that + clause" = noun phrase + that-clause as subject

questions.text: "She realised ___ the article was from a site with a known bias for publishing false stories."
questions.hint: "Realised that + clause" — that-clause after a cognitive verb

questions.text: "It is clear what disinformation is dangerous" is grammatically correct.
questions.hint: "It is clear THAT disinformation is dangerous" — "what" is wrong here

questions.text: "Understanding ___ filter bubbles form is crucial to addressing the problem." (the mechanism)
questions.hint: "How + S + V" = the mechanism/way in which something happens

questions.text: "It has been shown ___ fact-checking can reduce belief in false claims."
questions.hint: "It has been shown that + clause" — passive reporting + that-clause

questions.text: "Despite the fact ___ the story was false, it reached 10 million people before being corrected."
"___ she found was that the video had been manipulated." (noun clause as subject + direct object)
questions.hint: "What + S + V + was that…" = wh-clause as subject

questions.text: "It is essential ___ citizens develop critical media literacy skills." (formal recommendation)
Which sentence uses the noun clause correctly?
opts: "She believes what the story is false."
"It is evident that disinformation is a serious threat."
"That media literacy is important, it should be taught in schools."
questions.correct: "It is evident that disinformation is a serious threat."
questions.hint: "It is evident that + clause" = correct impersonal noun clause
